column1: 01 — IDENTITY & DESCRIPTION — Identify a manufacturer, reusable model, particular unit and API identity without collapsing them.

column7: [COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL/RELATED: ManufacturerName explicitly identifies the product producer; the TechnicalData use case can also treat a supplier as manufacturer. Retain a common manufacturer-information candidate, distinct from operator and instance identity. [Sources: AAS09-N014, AAS09-N015; F3-05-S06-R001]
column8: RELATED: BSI §6.2.5.15/Table32 declares ConfigurationData.manufacturer for the SAPIENT Node/interface component; not independently verified manufacturer of all installed physical instruments. [SAP03A-N12]

column7: [COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL/RELATED: ManufacturerProductDesignation, article number and order code support qualified product/model identification. Product designation text is not automatically a reusable model identifier; AssetKind and template kind remain different concepts. [Sources: AAS09-N015, AAS02-N011; F3-05-S06-R002]
column8: RELATED: BSI §6.2.5.15/Table32 ConfigurationData.model names the Node product, not a guaranteed model identifier for the whole installation or every physical subcomponent. [SAP03A-N12]
column9: [COMMON CANDIDATE] DIRECT: Model identifies the component model within its manufacturer product line. Product model designation is a reusable information need; this is a product kind, not an individual unit. [ISA21:S06-R002; F3-02]
column10: RELATED/PARTIAL: C239 §5.3 Procurable Unit, §6.3 FRU model, RF getModel/getEquipmentId, and PIC documentation use different product/part/instance scopes. None proves a model of an installed whole System. The 2022 DSDM distinguishes Product and ProductInstance but Product.name need not be a model number; C239 native equivalence unverified. [SOSA-D/G2-3/G2-4B/G2-6A/G3-N2]

column7: [COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL/RELATED: SpecificAssetId and AssetLink can carry a named serial number or other scoped asset identifier. Retain a common individual-identity candidate without equating serial, globalAssetId, product number or a verified installed unit. [Sources: AAS02-N012, AAS02-N009, AAS06-N006; F3-05-S06-R003]
column8: PARTIAL: BSI Table32 serial_number is conditional for hardware Nodes; pure-software Nodes may use product/license numbers. Not every Node serial is a physical equipment serial. [SAP03A-N12]
column9: [COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL: Serial Number identifies a component within its manufacturer/model; the combined manufacturer/model/serial is expected to be globally unique. A manufacturer-scoped serial is useful across equipment types, but the source does not verify a serial-numbered physical probe in any case. [ISA21:S06-R003; F3-02]
column10: RELATED: C239 §6.3 FRU inventory includes serial number but proves no installed case-equipment serial. NO_ESTABLISHED: an orderable fixed-pin-variant part number is not an individual serial number. [G2-3; G2-7Q §13.5.4.2.6.2]

column7: [COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL/RELATED: AAS Identifiable.id and represented-asset identifiers support distinct persistent identity roles. Preserve shell versus asset identity, scoped idShort and unprotected asset binding; neither an identifier nor an authenticated API proves the physical System identity. [Sources: AAS02-N018, AAS02-N009, AAS08-N042; F3-05-S06-R004]
column8: [COMMON CANDIDATE] RELATED: BSI §6.2.4 uses the same Node UUID across subsequent messages. This supports qualified persistent source identity; the timestamp conflict does not invalidate UUID meaning. Physical equipment identity and lifetime persistence are not established. [SAP02-N03, SAP03A-N03]
column9: [COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL: UCI is the string used persistently to refer to a specific ISA component; virtual components use qualified identifiers. Persistent component identity is a common need. Preserve ICD syntax/certificate association and CMPT virtual suffix rules as source constraints, not universal DIM rules. [ISA21:S06-R004; F3-02]
column10: [COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL: Sensor.elementID supports qualified sensing-entity identification. Its 2022 integer identifier has no established globally persistent URI or lifetime guarantee; those identity constraints remain held. A useful identifier candidate does not require exact ISA or OGC identity semantics. 2022 lineage; exact 2023 companion bytes unverified. [F3-04A-S06-R004]

column7: [COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL/RELATED: Part 4 defines issuer-key trust, signed access tokens and dataspace trust policy; public certificates are one permitted key source. This supports qualified trust-context information. Device certificate binding is only a possible approach, not a required equipment certificate or an authenticated physical identity. [Sources: AAS08-N033, AAS08-N041, AAS08-N042; F3-05-ISA-A-CERTIFICATE-TRUST]

[ICD-3.1.2, ICD-3.3, ICD-6.1, CERT-1.0, CERT-2.0, CERT-3.1, CERT-3.2, CERT-3.2.1, CERT-3.2.2, CERT-3.3, CERT-3.4; F3-06-ISA-ISA-A-CERTIFICATE-TRUST]

No mandatory ISA certificate Common Name, issuer/trust-anchor schema, or actual installed certificate is established. [G2-3/G2-5/G2-7R/G2-7S] SO-2D: root-of-trust may be hardware/software and cryptographic or design-based. The secure-startup authentication dependencies are preserved separately in SOSA-SO2D-SECURE-STARTUP; neither a certificate schema nor a successful authentication follows.

column1: 02 — SYSTEM, EQUIPMENT & RELATIONSHIPS — Describe the whole, physical constituents, separate connections, reporting participant and hosting context.

column7: [COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL/RELATED: A shell describes an asset through informational submodels; assets can include physical equipment and software. Retain a qualified described-system candidate while separating the represented asset, digital shell, design/type/instance context and actual sensing installation. [Sources: AAS02-N002, AAS03-N001, AAS09-N001; F3-05-S06-R005]
column8: RELATED: BSI Annex C describes an optional separately registered middleware Node participating in a SAPIENT network; neither the middleware nor the detected-object taxonomy defines one physical whole sensing assembly. [SAP06-N14,SAP06-N19]
column9: [SPECIALIZED CANDIDATE] PARTIAL: A Composition Interface Component (CIC) exposes a composition of members through an ISA interface. The optional architecture-specific integration arrangement is useful specialized information; it does not establish one physical assembly or a universal root. [ISA21:S06-R005; F3-02]
column10: [COMMON CANDIDATE] NARROWER/PARTIAL: C239 explicitly describes a sensing system containing one or more physical hardware elements, potentially spanning several modalities. This supports the common need to describe the sensing arrangement. Optional cards, chassis and software profiles do not erase that meaning or establish a universal DIM root or installed configuration. [F3-04A-S06-R005]

column7: [COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL/RELATED: Descriptors and endpoints identify API network resources and offered interfaces. They support common network-participant description on the same basis as logical ISA and SOSA participants; preserve optional shell endpoints, asset-versus-shell identity and unverified reachability. [AAS06-N003, AAS06-N004; F3-06-AAS-S06-R006]
column8: [COMMON CANDIDATE] RELATED: A SAPIENT Node is an identified architecture participant; optional middleware can also register as a Node. column9: [COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL: An ISA component or Controller is an interface-conformant network participant or service role. Describing the participant role is a common need; neither a physical sensor nor the original observation performer follows from network visibility. [ISA21:S06-R006; F3-02]
column10: [COMMON CANDIDATE] RELATED: C239 names interaction endpoints implemented by modules or hardware elements. These support describing a network participant independently of physical equipment identity. The modeled endpoint is not proof of live discovery, an independently exposed CSAPI System or an installed service. [F3-04A-S06-R006]

Design capability only, not a guaranteed installed endpoint or mandatory chassis. Original source IDs: SOSA-C239-TOC-6; SOSA-C239-G2-3-CONTEXT-OOB-LIGHTS-OUT; SOSA-C239-G2-3-CONTEXT-MANAGEMENT-TIERS; SOSA-C239-G2-3-CONTEXT-CHASSIS-MGR-PLACEMENT; SOSA-C239-G2-3-CONTEXT-HARDWARE-MANAGEMENT-INTERFACES. SO-2A: C239 §6 PDF64 also distinguishes managed from unmanaged components and direct from delegated supervision; capability/representation is separate from observed reachability. SO-2C: PDF104/111 permits management representation on another PIC and distinguishes direct/indirect/unmanaged cases. PDF100/103 defines a potentially restricted in-band IPMI command bridge to out-of-band management; neither feature proves a local endpoint or unrestricted CSAPI control. SO-2D: PDF123–124 permits distributed/redundant Chassis Managers and independent managers for distinct enclaves; subsidiary FRU representation and redundant channels do not imply one endpoint per card or observed reachability.
